sources.citation: Colin, Georges S. 1929. Le parler berbère des Ġmāra. Hespéris 9: 43-58 (archive.org scan of the volume, item hesperis-tamuda-1929_202511)
sources.note: Historical/ethnographic introduction on the Berber-speaking enclave plus two texts with French translation; no phonetic notes; scanned text a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/intensité/prosod with no hits.

sources.citation: Mourigh, Khalid. 2015. A grammar of Ghomara Berber. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LUCL), 566 pp. (repository 'Corrected Publisher's Version'; published as Rüdiger Köppe 2016).https://hdl.handle.net/1887/31685
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PJ2369.M6 M68 2016); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PJ2369.M6 M68 2016
sources.note: Chapter II Phonology (pp. 13-62: consonants, vowels incl. schwa, assimilation/sandhi, labialisation) has no section and no statement on word stress or accent; the words 'stress'/'accent' never occur in a phonological sense in the whole book. Only prosodic remarks: pharyngealisation spreads within 'the prosodic word which includes verbal and nominal clitics' (p. 40), and sentence intonation contours in the syntax chapters (e.g. yes/no questions marked by rising intonation on the predicate).

sources.citation: el Hannouche, Jamal. 2008. Ghomara Berber: A brief grammatical survey. MA thesis, Leiden University, 249 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Phonology chapter (pp. 28-42) covers consonant weakening, phonemic status of schwa and assimilations only; nothing on stress/accent ('stress' occurs only meaning 'emphasise').

sources.citation: el Hannouche, Jamal. 2010. Arabic influence in Ghomara Berber. MA thesis, Leiden University, 294 pp. (archive.org copy)
sources.note: Chapter I Phonology (same coverage as the 2008 thesis: consonant weakening, schwa, assimilation); scanned text a full-text search for stress/accent, nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Kossmann, Maarten & Harry Stroomer. 1997. Berber phonology. In Alan S. Kaye (ed.), Phonologies of Asia and Africa, vol. 2, 461-475. Winona Lake: Eisenbrauns.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Family-level phonological survey by the supervisor of the Ghomara descriptions; the likeliest place for a general statement on whether word stress is contrastive in Northern Berber, usable as a family-level fallback since the Ghomara grammar itself is silent (content not verified here).
